Repo: Tendril (current directory). Contest: how a page merges when two devices edit it. Main files: shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/tendril/app/sync/PagesSyncEngine.kt, PageSnapshotRecords.kt, data/page/Page.kt, Block.kt, PageRevision.kt, Property.kt, PageCanvas/CanvasNode/CanvasEdge, PageRelation, PurgedRecord.kt.
Claims (verify each; quote the rule):
1. A page travels as one snapshot file holding the page row, all its blocks, property values, labels, canvas nodes/edges and relations.
2. Merge is whole-page last-writer-wins on Page.updatedAt: the winning snapshot replaces every block of the page (delete and reinsert); nothing merges per block.
3. The losing body is kept as a PageRevision (reason MERGE) on the device where it lost, never synced; say how many revisions are kept and whether the person is told.
4. Two devices editing DIFFERENT blocks of the same page: one device's edit is lost from the live page (kept only in the revision). Quote the code path that proves it, or refute.
5. Block identity: blocks have a uid that travels; a block has no updatedAt or deletedAt of its own.
6. Page delete vs edit on another device: trash (deletedAt) is an ordinary field of the whole-row merge, so a later edit beats it; purge goes through PurgedRecord PAGE.
7. Canvas nodes and edges, database property values and page relations follow the same whole-page rule; say any that merge differently (e.g. PageDatabase rows as pages, properties purged separately).
